hypothesis: SQLite FTS5 with BM25 is a useful low-cost lexical baseline for messy memory retrieval.
notes: Bootstrap run; no prior champion. Established SQLite FTS5 + BM25 as the first champion.

hypothesis: IDF-weighted lexical coverage and a small exception-intent reranker improve BM25 ranking.
notes: No quality improvement; preserve Run 001 champion. Exception-intent heuristic needs held-out validation. Prior reported MRR 1.0 could not be reproduced with this reconstruction.
provenance: Reconstructed on 2026-10-06 from the prior conversation description. The original unpushed Run 002 patch was unavailable; these are fresh measurements, not the previously reported results.

hypothesis: A small generic source-authority and recency bonus can improve ranking over BM25 without increasing context size or storage.
notes: No retrieval-quality improvement. q011 remained rank 3 and q019 remained rank 2. Candidate added slight latency/CPU overhead, so Run 001 remains champion. Generic authority/recency priors alone were too weak to overcome lexical ambiguity on this benchmark.

hypothesis: Deterministic correction/supersession linking can remove stale retrieved memories without reducing retrieval quality.
notes: Accepted: unchanged retrieval quality with 1.95% lower mean returned context. Suppressed only explicitly stale notes linked to later corrections; all records remain stored for provenance.

hypothesis: A deterministic per-record context sketch can reduce prompt context while preserving retrieval quality and all retained content terms.
notes: Accepted: unchanged retrieval quality, 9.39% lower approximate context than Run 004, and 100% retention of non-function content terms. Full records remain indexed/stored; only assembled context is compacted.
resource_measurement_note: Connector runtime exposed compaction wall time but not comparable process CPU or peak RSS; the Python reproduction measures those metrics.

hypothesis: Run 005 compact context sketches preserve answer-bearing evidence on unseen queries while retaining their context reduction.
notes: Accepted as evaluation validation only. Run 005 remains champion. On 20 held-out queries compact context preserved 100% answer evidence and identical retrieval metrics versus full context while reducing approximate context by 9.53%.

hypothesis: Real Nomic vector-only retrieval improves relevance over the lexical champion on both frozen benchmarks.
notes: Reject vector-only challenger: original MRR 0.941667 -> 0.916667 and Hit@1 0.90 -> 0.85, despite Recall@5 improving 0.95 -> 0.975. Held-out retrieval/evidence unchanged, context larger and CPU/RAM/latency/storage higher. Preserve Run 005 as default; retain the reusable embedding harness for future models/hybrid tests.
Accepted as semantic-quality champion; Run 005 remains the lightweight no-embedding fallback due to the embedding resource cost.

hypothesis: BGE-small v1.5 can match Run 008 fixed-RRF semantic quality while materially reducing local embedding cost.
notes: Rejected as semantic-quality champion: the challenger did not match all Run 008 retrieval/evidence metrics with at least three measured resource improvements.

hypothesis: E5-small-v2 can match Run 008 fixed-RRF semantic quality while materially reducing local embedding cost.
notes: Accepted as semantic-quality champion: matched every Run 008 retrieval/evidence metric and reduced at least three of model size, RSS and latency.

hypothesis: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 can match Run 010 fixed-RRF quality while further reducing local embedding cost.
notes: Rejected as semantic-quality champion: the challenger did not match all Run 10 retrieval/evidence metrics with at least three measured resource improvements.

hypothesis: Dynamic INT8 E5-small-v2 can preserve Run 010 quality while reducing model, memory and latency costs.
notes: Rejected as semantic-quality champion: the challenger did not match all Run 10 retrieval/evidence metrics with at least three measured resource improvements.

hypothesis: Nomic's documented 256-dimensional Matryoshka projection can preserve fixed-RRF retrieval quality while reducing vec0 storage.
notes: Rejected as semantic-quality champion: the challenger did not match all Run 10 retrieval/evidence metrics with at least three measured resource improvements.

hypothesis: A fixed query-aware clause selector can reduce Run 010 context without changing retrieval or losing held-out evidence.
notes: Accepted as the context-assembly extension to Run 10: retrieval/evidence metrics matched and context fell on both frozen sets.

hypothesis: A fixed conservative cross-record near-duplicate clause filter can reduce Run 014 context while preserving quality, evidence, and source provenance.
notes: Rejected: the fixed conservative rule did not reduce context on both frozen sets while preserving quality, provenance, and acceptable assembly latency.

hypothesis: A fixed 128-token rank-aware budget can reduce Run 014 context while preserving retrieval quality, held-out evidence, and provenance.

budget_rule.additional_clause_order: retrieval rank, then selected clause order
budget_rule.mandatory: first Run 014 selected clause from every retrieved record
budget_rule.mandatory_overflow: retain mandatory clauses even if they exceed the budget
budget_rule.overflow: stop admitting optional clauses before the first overflow; never truncate a clause
budget_rule.provenance: record every retained and omitted source record, rank, and selected-clause index

notes: Rejected: the fixed budget did not reduce context on both frozen sets while preserving quality, provenance, and acceptable assembly latency.

hypothesis: Protecting every selected clause in the rank-one record before applying Run 016's fixed 128-token target can retain evidence while reducing Run 014 context.
notes: Accepted as the context-assembly extension to Run 14: retrieval/evidence metrics matched and context fell on both frozen sets.

hypothesis: sqlite-vec unit-range int8 storage can preserve Run 017 quality and context while reducing SQLite vector storage without changing FP32 E5 inference.

vector_storage.query_quantization: same sqlite-vec unit quantizer immediately before search

notes: Rejected as a vector-storage extension to Run 17: it did not preserve quality/context with smaller SQLite storage and sub-2 ms vector search.

hypothesis: Per-vector symmetric max-absolute int8 scaling can preserve Run 017 quality and context while retaining Run 018's SQLite storage reduction.

vector_storage.query_quantization: same deterministic per-vector max-absolute rule immediately before search
vector_storage.scale_storage: not required because cosine distance is invariant to positive per-vector scaling

notes: Rejected as a vector-storage extension to Run 17: it did not preserve quality/context with smaller SQLite storage and sub-2 ms vector search.

hypothesis: Max-absolute int8 vec0 candidate retrieval followed by FP16 reranking can match Run 017 quality and context with substantially less SQLite storage.

vector_storage.candidate_index: sqlite-vec int8[384] with per-vector max-absolute scaling
vector_storage.query_quantization: max-absolute int8 for candidate search; FP32 for reranking
vector_storage.rerank_corpus_precision: float16 storage converted to float32 for scoring
vector_storage.rerank_distance: cosine computed in FP32 from stored FP16 corpus vectors and FP32 query

notes: Accepted as the vector-storage extension to Run 17: retrieval/evidence and context matched while SQLite storage fell and mean vector search stayed below 2 ms.

hypothesis: A content-addressed SQLite embedding cache can avoid unchanged-document inference and limit a one-record update to one embedding while preserving Run 020 retrieval.
notes: Accepted as the embedding-cache extension to Run 20: retrieval/evidence/context matched, warm reindex avoided all inference, and the one-record update embedded only one document within the fixed storage limit.

hypothesis: Embedding-convention namespaces can prevent stale cache reuse and permit bounded cleanup without changing Run 021 retrieval or active-cache hits.
notes: Accepted as the cache-maintenance extension to Run 21: convention namespaces prevented stale reuse, cleanup retained the active cache, and retrieval/evidence/context matched.

hypothesis: A durable SQLite pending queue can make records immediately FTS5-searchable, drain embeddings in bounded FIFO batches with cache reuse, and converge to Run 022 retrieval.
notes: Accepted as the pending-ingestion extension to Run 22: FTS5 remained available before model loading, the bounded FIFO worker reused cache entries, and final retrieval/evidence/context matched.

hypothesis: A reopened SQLite worker can reclaim a durably stranded processing batch and complete with unique ready outputs while preserving Run 023 retrieval.

recovery.interruption_point: after processing commit and before cache lookup or inference

notes: Accepted as the pending-recovery extension to Run 23: four durably stranded processing jobs survived reopen, were reclaimed, completed with unique ready outputs, and final retrieval/evidence/context matched.

hypothesis: A pending document update can supersede its stale embedding job, expose only the latest FTS5 content, and attach only the newest vector and cache key while preserving Run 024 retrieval.
notes: Rejected as a pending-supersession extension to Run 24: latest-content provenance, stale-job isolation, final parity, or a resource gate failed.

hypothesis: The asynchronous pending-supersession path can exactly reproduce an independently embedded synchronous reindex of the same declared update, separating queue correctness from natural content drift.
notes: Accepted as the pending-supersession synchronous-control extension to Run 24: the asynchronous path exactly matched an independently embedded synchronous reindex for FTS5, vector-only, hybrid, context, and vectors while preserving lifecycle and resource bounds.

hypothesis: Two local workers using independent SQLite connections and atomic claims can process disjoint batches exactly once while preserving Run 026 output.
notes: Accepted as the two-worker atomic-claim extension to Run 26: independent SQLite connections claimed disjoint FIFO batches exactly once, completed unique attachments, and preserved vectors, retrieval, evidence, context, and resource bounds.

hypothesis: Text-only FP32 EmbeddingGemma 2 can improve the current E5 champion's retrieval without evidence/context loss or unacceptable CPU, memory, latency or storage growth.
notes: EmbeddingGemma 2 text-only FP32 was evaluated locally using the pinned community ONNX export and the current fixed SQLite/RRF/context pipeline. Retain reusable infrastructure; keep E5 as default unless every predeclared replacement gate passes.
